speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Manpower in view of the estimated cost of informal caregiving in Singapore valued at $1.28 billion, whether the Government has studied or will the Government be studying the number of people who (i) are carrying out unpaid caregiving and their age range; (ii) quit their full-time jobs to conduct unpaid caregiving and their age range and (iii) may not have the means to support themselves when they themselves become seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We recognise the importance of supporting caregivers in terms of their employment and retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: There are various job placement and skills upgrading measures for those who wish to return to work, as well as Central Provident Fund support schemes to boost their retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We will continue to review our efforts, so that there will be adequate support for caregivers who are vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Has the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) conducted any studies regarding the impact on the productivity and long-term competitiveness of our workforce, when an increasing number of residents need to quit full-time work or reduce working hours in order to perform unpaid caregiving for their loved ones?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: What measures have been considered to mitigate these effects on workers and the economy, including allocating more resources to paid caregiving?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And on that note, will the Ministry consider establishing a paid family care leave scheme, modelled after the childcare leave scheme, to provide caregiving leave to employees who are the primary caregivers for elderly parents or family members with disabilities?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: For example, the first three days could be paid for by employers and the remaining three days paid for by the Government.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will go some way to help improve the quality of life, economic security and productivity of working caregivers.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We are mindful that caregiving will be an increased trend amongst our adult population, especially since by 2030, one in four local residents would be above 65 years old.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, they are many measures that the Government is taking to make the caregiving responsibility more manageable for families.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: On one hand, we are looking at daycare centres, institutions, home care and caregiver respite programmes to make the caregiving a shared responsibility, something for which there are external groups that families can turn to.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: On the work front, it would certainly be a strain on people who are working and who also have to take care of either seniors, or young children, or vulnerable families at the same time.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: That is why we have been working very hard to encourage workplaces to have flexible work arrangements, so that there will be better feasibility for caregivers to still be able to continue to work.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: And thus far, the trend has been quite stable and healthy.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: In fact, for women, I am very happy to say that the employment rate has actually grown, despite the increase in caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: On the second supplementary question about family care leave, I suppose that the Member is referring to leave given to employees who have to take care of children or senior family members.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We have actually enhanced the leave for parents to take care of infants.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Next year onwards, shared parental leave as well as paternity leave will be enhanced.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I think that is good news and we seek not just employers', but co-workers' and also the community's support for parents with young children.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: As for employees who have to take care of seniors, we recognise that caregiving for parents is an important responsibility and even without any legislated mandatory requirement or financial incentives to do so, many progressive employers here have stepped up to introduce caregiving-related leave provisions beyond what is currently mandated, as part of the human resources' strategy to attract and retain talent.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Going forward, we will certainly want to work more closely with the industry, as well as with employers, to look at other ways that we can support employees who have caregiving needs for the elderly.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate the Minister of State's response and also the whole myriad of flexible work arrangements and improvements that we are forging in society.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: But I think there is a significant subset of caregivers who are in situations where both their parents are down with very difficult health conditions, where there is absolutely no option for them to just take on the part-time caregiver role.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This number, we do not know how big it is, but for the families and the caregivers who are in that situation, they really suffer significant financial impact for the number of years lost that they are not able to work.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I have residents who are in their 40s who are in this predicament, so I have actually been championing for Carefare for the past four years in Parliament.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask for an update – whether MOM would consider studying what this number of highly impacted families are, maybe by way of additional questions in the national census, to find out and identify these group of families who are very vulnerable because of intense care needs and where no extent of flexible work arrangements is feasible for them.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: And I think there is more that ought to be done, if the Home Caregiving Grant, by itself, is not sufficient.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: On the MOH front, I understand there are also schemes to make caregiving more affordable, alternative caregiving support, instead of just relying on family members quitting their jobs to support the elderly family members.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: On the data portion, I think we will work closely with MOH to monitor as well as to analyse the trend of the profile of caregivers, understanding that there are many archetypes out there and that we do want to provide more targeted support for each archetype of caregiver.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: The Minister of State said that many progressive employers have implemented caregiving leave.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, why not legislate it, so that all employers, whether progressive or less progressive, will provide caregiving leave for their employees?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: In the meantime, can the Government provide more financial and non-financial incentives to employers who provide caregiving leave for their employees?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: And secondly, can the Minister of State provide any details on any plans or initiatives by MOM to assist individuals who have taken on unpaid caregiving responsibilities and now ready to reintegrate into the workforce once their caregiving responsibilities are over?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We certainly welcome caregivers who want to return to work to tap on all this support that is available.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: On working with employers to mandate caregiving leave, as suggested by Mr Gerald Giam, there are many types of leave provisions that we are working with the industry on, to support the various needs of employees.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: As I mentioned earlier on, we have just enhanced the paternity leave as well as the shared parental leave and that is to cater to parents with young children.
